# 10 Best AI Tools for Marketers in 2026 — Boost Your Campaigns

Marketers, get ready to work 10x faster with AI! Here are our top picks for 2026!

For more tools, check out our [[link:/category/Productivity|Productivity category]] and [[link:/category/Writing|Writing category]]!

---

## Quick Comparison Table

| Tool | Best For | Pricing | Key Features |
|------|-----------|---------|---------------|
| [[link:/tools/18|Jasper]] | Long-form & SEO writing | $49+/month | 60+ templates, brand voice |
| [[link:/tools/74|Copy.ai]] | Short-form marketing copy | $36+/month | 90+ templates, free tier |
| [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] | Marketing video creation | $12+/month | Auto-subtitles, text-to-video |
| Pika Labs | Creative social videos | Free beta | Generative video, styles |
| [[link:/tools/2|DALL-E 3]] | Marketing images | $0.04+/image | Photorealistic, text rendering |
| [[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]] | On-page SEO scoring | $89+/month | SERP analysis, content score |
| [[link:/tools/22|Writesonic]] | Ad & landing page copy | $16+/month | Templates, SEO article writer |
| [[link:/tools/87|Gamma]] | Decks and one-pagers | Free tier | Outline-to-deck, web export |
| [[link:/tools/58|Frase]] | Content briefs & research | $15+/month | SERP question extraction |
| [[link:/tools/10|Perplexity AI]] | Competitor & market research | Free tier | Cited real-time answers |

---

## 1. Jasper (Best for Long-form and Brand Voice)

[[link:/tools/18|Jasper]] is built for teams publishing at volume. Its brand voice feature learns your existing copy so drafts do not need a full rewrite to sound like you.

Best for blog posts, email sequences, and consistent brand messaging! The practical setup is to feed it three or four published pieces as a voice reference before generating anything client-facing.

---

## 2. Copy.ai (Best for Short-form Copy)

[[link:/tools/74|Copy.ai]] covers the high-volume, low-ceremony end of marketing: social posts, ad variations, product descriptions.

Social posts, ad copy, product descriptions — all fast and easy! The workflow that saves the most time is generating twenty variants of one ad, then cutting to the four worth testing rather than trying to write the perfect line first.

---

## 3. VEED.io (Best for Marketing Videos)

[[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] handles the editing work that eats a marketing afternoon: auto-subtitles, trimming, resizing for each platform.

Create professional marketing videos, social reels, and explainer videos in minutes! Auto-captions matter more than they look — most feeds autoplay silent, so a video without burned-in subtitles loses most of its audience.

---

## 4. Pika Labs (Best for Creative Video)

Pika Labs generates short stylised clips from a prompt or an image, which suits scroll-stopping social creative.

For stylized, eye-catching social media videos! Treat it as a source of distinctive B-roll and hooks rather than a replacement for product footage — generated clips still look generated, and viewers notice.

---

## 5. DALL-E 3 (Best for Marketing Imagery)

[[link:/tools/2|DALL-E 3]] follows long prompts closely and, unusually, renders legible text inside images.

Create product mockups, social graphics, and banner ads! That text rendering is the reason to pick it over most image models for anything with a headline on it, though you should still check spelling — it gets close, not perfect.

---

## 6. SurferSEO (Best for On-page SEO)

[[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]] scores a draft against the pages currently ranking for your target query, then tells you what is missing.

Use it after the draft exists, not before. Writing to a score from the start produces stiff copy; drafting first and then closing the gaps gives you something that both ranks and reads.

---

## 7. Writesonic (Best for Ad and Landing Page Copy)

[[link:/tools/22|Writesonic]] sits between Jasper and Copy.ai on price, with templates aimed at ads, landing pages and SEO articles.

A good use is churning out landing page variants for paid campaigns. Ship three headlines and two body versions per campaign, then let the ad platform decide which one survives.

---

## 8. Gamma (Best for Decks and One-pagers)

[[link:/tools/87|Gamma]] turns an outline into a designed deck, and exports it as a web page you can send instead of a PDF attachment.

Useful for client proposals and campaign recaps. You write the headings, it handles layout — and the web export means you can update a deck after sending it.

---

## 9. Frase (Best for Content Briefs)

[[link:/tools/58|Frase]] reads the current search results for a query and extracts the questions and headings real pages cover.

Hand the output to whoever is writing. Briefs built from actual SERP data remove the guesswork from "what should this article include", which is where most content projects stall.

---

## 10. Perplexity AI (Best for Competitor and Market Research)

[[link:/tools/10|Perplexity AI]] answers research questions with sources attached to every claim.

Use it for competitor pricing, category trends and analyst summaries before a campaign. Every line carries a citation you can open, which is what makes the output safe to quote in a strategy doc.

---

## How to Pick Without Burning Budget

Ten tools is more than any marketer needs. A workable stack for a small team:

- **One writing tool** — Jasper for brand-led long form, or Writesonic if budget is tighter.
- **One video tool** — VEED.io for editing, plus Pika for creative experiments.
- **One research tool** — Perplexity for market questions, SurferSEO or Frase if organic search is the channel that matters.

Run each on its free tier for two weeks before paying. The failure mode is subscribing to four tools in one enthusiastic afternoon and using one of them.

---

## FAQ

**Which tool should a solo marketer start with?**
Copy.ai or Writesonic for copy, plus Perplexity for research. That covers most daily work under $20 a month.

**Do AI images need disclosure?**
Policies vary by platform and region. If a campaign is paid or the image depicts a real person or product, check the platform's rules before publishing.

**Will AI copy hurt SEO?**
Not inherently. Thin, unedited, duplicated copy does — which is a drafting problem, not a tooling one.
